answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making every fake identity climb its own knoll. Each new account posts a bond that doubles with every account sharing its funding trail: the first costs 1 unit, the tenth costs 512. A gale of cheap clones dies on that curve, since each extra clone only multiplies the bill. To block bulk farming, each bond needs a live review by an independent auditor at an unpredictable time, paid with outside money the auditor keeps either way. That cash buys no useful signal in return: the review asks novel questions in real time that cannot be scripted in bulk.
